title: The battle you’re losing might not be spiritual warfare.
paragraphs:
The battle you’re losing might not be spiritual warfare.
It might be something buried under your tent.
In Book of Joshua 7, after Jericho fell, Israel was unstoppable. Walls down. Promise unfolding. God’s power undeniable.
Then one man saw what glittered.
A robe from Shinar. Silver. Gold.
God had already spoken: Don’t take it.
He took it anyway.

He hid it.
Buried it.
Under his tent.
No lightning. No sirens. Just quiet soil covering quiet rebellion.
Then they marched to Ai — and were crushed.
Men died. Courage melted. Leaders panicked. Worship turned to weeping.
One man’s hidden sin became a nation’s public defeat.
That’s the part we don’t like.
Because we prefer private compromise and public anointing.

But hidden sin leaks.
Into marriages.
Into ministries.
Into leadership decisions.
Into worship atmospheres.
God didn’t expose Achan because He loves shame.
He exposed him because He protects covenant.
And here’s the mercy:
Where Achan buried sin in the earth, Jesus carried sin on a tree.
Where secrecy brought judgment, the Cross brings mercy.
“Be sure your sin will find you out.” — Book of Numbers 32:23
But also:
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us.” — First Epistle of John 1:9

Exposure is not God destroying you.
Exposure is God refusing to let hidden rot destroy the camp.
Let me ask you honestly, kapatid:
What’s under your tent?

Bitterness nobody sees?
A secret addiction?
Financial compromise?
Pride disguised as “calling”?
Don’t wait for Ai to fall.
Bring it into the light.
Because Jesus doesn’t expose to crush you.
He exposes to cleanse you.
And a clean camp fights differently.
